change_policy.replacement: each hcode revision replaces this manifest in place and changes its semantics hash; Worker and Nodepool builds must be upgraded together

tensor_operation_units.freivalds_check: per round: cols + inner*(cols + 1) + rows*(1 + inner + cols), summed over rounds, where a is rows by inner, b is inner by cols, and c is rows by cols
tensor_operation_units.matmul: one unit per output row, one per output position, and one per multiply-add: m + m*n + m*k*n
tensor_operation_units.position_rule: elementwise, reshape, transpose, cast, sum, tolist, tensor, zeros, index, relu, gelu, and softmax charge the positions they visit, which is walk_count of the operand's shape, times their per-position units

vectors.name: single-return-function
vectors.source: fn id(x) { return x; } return id(7);

known_limitations.statement: Arithmetic results must remain within signed i64. The evaluator uses checked arithmetic and reports overflow as a failed execution. Code that intends two's-complement wrap-around must call wrapping_add, wrapping_sub, or wrapping_mul.

Call depth, value size, collection size, value depth, materialization size, source size, input size, output size, and task deadline remain bounded safety limits. Only operation and loop counters are not fixed work limits in v1.

Source string literals are byte-decoded and therefore do not preserve non-ASCII UTF-8. They also do not accept \uXXXX or surrogate escape syntax; only quote, backslash, newline, carriage-return, and tab escapes are recognized. JSON input and canonical output remain UTF-8.
A budget-exhausted replica is failed for consensus purposes, but accepted work recorded before exhaustion remains a Nodepool settlement input.

The CPU transcendental builtins are reproducible but not correctly rounded. On the tested grids their worst observed errors are 4 ulp for ln and tanh, 3 ulp for exp, sin, and cos, and 33 ulp for pow. pow's error grows with |exponent * ln(base)|, so large products can lose more digits.

semantics.budget_policy: max_cpt is a positive per-replica execution-credit allowance; execution stops before charging an operation that would exceed it
semantics.canonical_output: top-level strings are raw UTF-8; other values are compact JSON with sorted dict keys
semantics.float_math: sqrt, floor, ceil, round, abs, min, max, float, and int use IEEE-754 or exact operations. exp, ln, sin, cos, tanh, and pow use fixed software series that never call the host libm. sin and cos accept |x| <= 1000000, ln and pow of a negative base with a non-integral exponent fail, and int fails outside the int64 range. Integral pow exponents with magnitude at most 64 use repeated squaring, inverting the base first for negative exponents to preserve representable subnormal results.
semantics.float_model: IEEE-754 binary64 with round-to-nearest-even. Every CPU hcode float is finite: an operation whose result is NaN or infinite fails the execution, and -0.0 is folded to 0.0. Float literals and JSON numbers must be finite.
semantics.freivalds_check: freivalds_check(a, b, c, seed, rounds) returns true when a * (b * r) equals c * r for the 0/1 vector r of every round. Each round's vector comes from a splitmix64 stream that starts at seed. a, b, and c must be i64 matrices with shapes m by k, k by n, and m by n, with every entry in the i32 range, and rounds must be 1 through 64. A correct product always passes. A wrong product passes one round with probability at most 1/2 when the round vector is uniformly random, so it passes all rounds with probability at most 2^-rounds under that idealization. The theoretical bound requires independent uniform vectors independent of the fixed claim; a verifier fixes the claim before choosing an unpredictable independent challenge. This builtin uses deterministic splitmix64 with a 64-bit seed and has no proven adversarial 2^-rounds soundness guarantee. It is a diagnostic check, not Nodepool verification or a substitute for replica consensus.
semantics.integer_remainder: % truncates like /: the result takes the sign of the dividend; a zero divisor fails, and i64::MIN % -1 fails in checked mode
semantics.integer_shift: << and >> require a count in 0 through 63; << discards bits shifted out of the 64-bit word; >> is arithmetic
semantics.source_comments: CPU hcode only. // starts a comment that runs to the end of its line. Inside a string literal, // is ordinary text, and a single / is division.
semantics.source_control_flow: CPU hcode only. while, break, continue, and if are keywords there; on the frozen v0 surface they stay ordinary names. while condition { statements } checks a bool condition before each entry to its body, and a non-bool condition fails with type_error. Each entry counts as one loop iteration against max_loop_iterations, the same counter as for. break; ends the innermost for or while loop, and continue; ends the current pass through its body. if condition { statements } else { statements } runs one branch; the else part is optional and may be another if. Where an expression statement could start with if, the if is read as a statement when its branches are statements, and otherwise as an expression, as before. A function body starts a new loop context, so break and continue outside a loop, including inside a function body, are parse errors. Every statement and expression is charged as before, and a while condition is charged on every check.
semantics.tensor_artifacts: CPU hcode accepts execution-local SHA-256-pinned safetensors bytes, never filesystem paths or URLs. load_tensor(artifact, name) decodes an entire tensor; load_tensor_slice(artifact, name, offset, shape) decodes a contiguous row-major element slice; tensor_info(artifact, name) returns the storage dtype and shape. Supported storage dtypes are I8, U8, I16, I32, I64, F16, BF16, F32, and F64; integer values become i64 and floats become finite, positive-zero-normalized f64. Rank is 1 through 8. Headers reject duplicate tensors/fields, overlapping ranges, holes, trailing bytes, and shape/length mismatches. Artifacts are bounded separately from JSON input. Decoded values remain subject to all existing collection, value, materialization, output, and CPT limits. Loads charge one unit per selected shape position before decoding; tensor_info charges one per dimension. Header/digest validation is bounded host-side admission work, like JSON parsing, not interpreter executed_ops. No artifact output or arbitrary host I/O is exposed.
semantics.tensor_model: Immutable row-major tensors of rank 1 through 8 with dtype i64 or f64. Canonical output is an object with sorted keys, {"data":[...],"dtype":"f64","shape":[...]}. Tensors are created only by the tensor builtins; JSON input never produces them. Elementwise + - * / require equal shapes or one scalar operand, and mixed dtypes promote to f64. Integer tensor arithmetic is checked, and float tensor elements must stay finite. Tensors support == and != structurally and have no ordering operators. Every tensor shape must satisfy walk_count <= max_collection_items, where walk_count is the product of its dimensions with each zero dimension counted as one. The check runs before any storage is reserved, so zero-size tensors cannot hide large dimensions. tensor(list) charges the inferred shape positions before collecting or converting leaves.
